text: They built a wooden ___ near the forest.
why: 'built a wooden home' is also standard (AmE real-estate sense of home = house)

text: Our neighbours sold their ___ last month.
why: 'sold their home' is equally common

text: He rented a small ___ with three bedrooms.
why: 'a small home with three bedrooms' is also standard

text: The estate agent showed us a brick ___ in the suburbs.
why: 'a brick home in the suburbs' is also standard estate-agent language

text: They are planning to buy a ___ with a pool.
why: 'buy a home with a pool' is equally natural

text: A ___ costs much more in the capital than in the countryside.
why: 'A home costs more...' is also natural (housing-market sense)

text: We usually ___ a film on Friday evenings.
why: 'see a film' is also correct

text: She likes to ___ birds in the park.
why: 'likes to see birds' is also acceptable

text: Don't ___ down on people who are different.
why: only works through the phrasal idiom 'look down on', not covered by the hint

text: Come and ___ our team practise on Saturday.
why: 'Come and see our team practise' is equally correct

text: The first test was hard, and ___ one was harder.
why: unnatural: the second test needs 'the second/the next one'; 'another' reads oddly

text: Has the bus arrived ___?
why: 'Has the bus arrived already?' is also correct (surprise)

text: It is ten o'clock, and she is ___ sleeping.
why: 'already sleeping' works if it is 10 p.m.; time of day not given

text: Have you chosen a gift ___?
why: 'Have you chosen a gift already?' is also correct

text: Share the sweets ___ the three children.
why: 'share between' for dividing among individuals is standard, esp. BrE

text: He found an old coin ___ the sand.
why: unnatural: a coin is found 'in the sand', not 'among' it (sand is a mass)

text: Lena's laugh stood out ___ the noise of the crowd.
why: unnatural: idiomatic is 'above/over the noise'; 'among the noise' is odd

text: Good teachers ___ with patience.
why: leak: 'teachers' gives away 'teach'

text: Please ___ chapter five for tomorrow.
why: 'learn chapter five for tomorrow' (memorise) is also natural

text: Which subject do you ___ at school?
why: 'Which subject do you learn at school?' is also common

text: The ___ app on my phone works without internet.
why: 'vocabulary app' (flashcard app) is also a real, natural phrase

text: He mentioned the ___ of moving to Prague.
why: 'the opportunity of moving to Prague' (e.g. job offer) is also fine

text: Vacuuming and dusting are typical ___.
why: grammar: uncountable 'housework' after plural 'are typical' is awkward; needs 'housework tasks/chores'

text: The bakery is closed ___ the holidays.
why: 'closed for the holidays' is equally correct

text: The sofa seems to ___ when you sit down.
why: extended meaning outside the hint, and odd: you sink into the sofa, the sofa doesn't sink

text: The sun will ___ behind the hills soon.
why: figurative meaning not covered by the hint (go down under water)

text: My heart began to ___ when I saw the exam.
why: idiom 'my heart sank', not covered by the hint

text: Sailors ___ across the ocean for weeks.
why: leak: 'Sailors' gives away 'sail'

text: On a windy day, it is perfect to ___.
why: unnatural grammar: 'it is perfect for sailing / perfect weather to sail'

text: The medicine did not ___ to help him.
why: 'did not fail to help' means it did help - confusing/unnatural; intended 'failed to help'
